# User description Closes #3490 ## What changed - require a durable qualifying-entry marker before server-assigned guided first sessions - fail closed for migrated or stale quiz state while preserving explicit QA routes - add persistence, eligibility, repeated-launch, and regression-plan coverage ## Verification - SwiftFormat: clean - generic iOS Simulator product build: passed - pre-review focused/native proof: 125/125 passed across the focused pack and four native journeys at `d179f2c2a7ac54ed3835284fd5fcf76188e36ebe` - pre-review TestFlight: 4.37.1 (1756), Xcode Cloud run `ec92f4c8-f6c0-47d1-bf23-b0670c81004b`, `VALID`, `INTERNAL_ONLY`, `IN_BETA_TESTING` - current review-remediation head: `c9fa0ad0b16aeae7de690ce13a062779e0c771fc`; fresh focused/native/TestFlight revalidation is queued - visual evidence: evidence-ready/transfer-pending; the exact Figma node read is currently blocked by connector reauthentication --- # Generated description Persist a durable guided-first-session admission marker in AtlyPlusPersonalizationService and enforce it in GuidedFirstSessionService so only qualifying long-quiz entrants can reach the guided flow, with migrated state falling back as unqualifiedEntry. Route token-based account switching through LogoutService and RootViewModel so logout clears account-scoped personalization before a new session starts, while UI-test helpers and regression coverage keep explicit QA paths available.

reviews.body:
The approach is right — a durable admission marker that fails closed for migrated state is the correct shape for this fix, and the migration details are handled well (`Bool?` in the QA backup struct so old payloads still decode, `eraseCachedData()` clears the marker, both profile-menu QA reset paths clear it).

Two blocking items before this lands, both commented inline:

1. The new guard sits **above** the `.consumed` guard, so users who legitimately completed the guided journey on 4.36/4.37 now resolve `.unqualifiedEntry` instead of `.consumed` after upgrade. That corrupts the exact analytics readout #3490 names as its success metric, and it flips `shouldSuppressExistingHomeTooltips` for that cohort. One-line fix.
2. `testEstablishedUserWithMigratedQuizStateNeverReentersGuidedFirstSession` asserts `.exists` synchronously against an asynchronously-resolved overlay, so it can pass even with the gate removed. This is the PR's central regression proof and the test the amended ONB-005 row now points at.

Two non-blocking questions:

**Repeat-presentation for genuinely eligible users.** `markConsumed()` is only reached from `FollowUpResultsSheetViewModel.swift:2678`, i.e. after the guided search reaches `.results` with non-empty cards. A qualifying new user who sees the hero and kills the app before results load never sets `consumed`, and the new marker stays `true` forever — so the walkthrough re-presents on every launch. That's the same symptom #3490 reports, for the other cohort. #3490 lists "Ensure repeated launches do not re-present the walkthrough after exclusion or consumption" under Requirements and "Eligible new long-quiz users still receive the journey exactly once" under Acceptance Criteria, but also puts "Walkthrough progress persistence after backgrounding" out of scope. Could you state explicitly which side of that line this falls on, rather than leaving it implicit?

**Verification evidence.** `AtlyTests` and `AtlyUITests` do not run on PR checks (AtlyPRSmoke is a fixed allowlist), so none of the tests added here execute in CI — the 125/125 result is a local run only. `Atly | Feature PR Checks` is still `pending` as of this review, so the product-build claim is also unconfirmed here. Separately, `docs/exec-plans/active/3490-guided-first-session-eligibility.md` ships with every acceptance criterion and every verification row marked `pending` and `last_updated: 2026-07-31`, which contradicts the PR description's "focused native proof / TestFlight VALID" claims at an Aug 2 head. Please reconcile the doc with the body before merge.

Minor, take or leave: `isExplicitTestAssignment` rebuilds a subset of `allowedAssignmentSources` on every call (a pair of `static let` `Set<String>` would drop the duplication and the linear scans); and `restoreRelease436StateAfterInternalQA`'s `?? false` means a QA backup captured on an older build silently drops admission on restore.

meta.title: Fix repeated guided first sessions for existing users

nodes.body:
**Blocking — this guard needs to sit below the `.consumed` check.**

Guard order in `resolveHero` is now `missingLongQuiz → unqualifiedAssignment → unqualifiedEntry → missingExposure → consumed`. A user who legitimately completed the guided first session on 4.36/4.37 has `hasConsumedGuidedFirstSession() == true` and no admission marker, so on upgrade they short-circuit here and report `.unqualifiedEntry` — never reaching the `.consumed` guard on line 298.

Two consequences:

**Analytics.** `FollowUpResultsSheetViewModel.swift:1335` emits `eligibilityResolved` for every reason except `gateOff`/`missingLongQuiz`, so `unqualified_entry` will swallow the entire already-consumed cohort. #3490 names `app_first_session_guided_eligibility_resolved` with `reason_family` as the readout for verifying this fix and asks that reason families distinguish established-user paths — this ordering makes that readout unable to separate "never qualified" from "already had it."

**UI.** `shouldSuppressExistingHomeTooltips` (`FollowUpResultsSheetViewModel.swift:449-462`) returns `true` for `.consumed` but `false` for `.unqualifiedEntry`. Consumed users therefore flip from suppressed to un-suppressed and become eligible for the legacy Home tooltips at `FollowUpResultsSheetView.swift:2220` and `:2229`. Blast radius is bounded by `userRepository.hasSeenHomeRootCategoryTooltip()`, but users who never saw those tips *because* the guided flow suppressed them will now start getting them.

Either move the `consumed` guard above this one, or treat consumption as implying admission:

```swift
guard isExplicitTestAssignment
    || personalizationService.hasQualifyingGuidedFirstSessionEntry()
    || personalizationService.hasConsumedGuidedFirstSession()
else { return .fallback(.unqualifiedEntry) }
```

Worth a unit case pinning it: consumed state + no marker should resolve `.fallback(.consumed)`, not `.fallback(.unqualifiedEntry)`.

Commit c9fa0ad **addressed** this comment by placing the `.consumed` guard before the new `.unqualifiedEntry` guard. Consumed users without an admission marker now resolve as `.consumed` instead of `.unqualifiedEntry`.

Addressed in `c9fa0ad0b16aeae7de690ce13a062779e0c771fc`. The consumed guard now runs after exposure but before the qualifying-entry fallback, preserving `.consumed` analytics and tooltip semantics for upgraded users. The focused unit matrix now pins consumed state plus no marker to `.fallback(.consumed)`. Fresh exact-head native revalidation is queued; I am leaving the thread open until that proof returns.

Current-head proof has returned green for `c9fa0ad0b16aeae7de690ce13a062779e0c771fc`. The focused unit pack passed **131/131** with zero failures/skips and includes the consumed-without-marker case resolving to `.fallback(.consumed)`. The exact-head Feature PR check is also green. Durable native receipt SHA-256: `2b6f745d78e8c35f1d3fc5ef38b2b54c228ad55da613ca6aba65f364fba7856d` (evidence index SHA-256: `69c4ec3788f908c15d34efbd17317fee58afc0b64d010cdbce87ac51ffa7bfe2`). Resolving this addressed thread.

**Blocking — this assertion can pass even if the gate is removed.**

Hero resolution is asynchronous: map camera → `resolveHero` → network. The positive test for the same identifier at line 736 allows `waitForExistence(timeout: 15)`, so the hero legitimately takes seconds to appear after Home renders. Checking `.exists` synchronously the instant `"Trending collections"` shows up therefore proves nothing — revert the `GuidedFirstSessionService` change and this test still goes green unless the timing happens to line up.

There's also no assertion that the fixture actually applied. If `-UITestSeedUnqualifiedGuidedFirstSessionState` silently fails to seed (wrong launch-arg plumbing, ordering in `applyTestingConfiguration`, etc.), the test reads green for the wrong reason. `UITestHelperTests` covers the seeding in isolation, but nothing ties that to what the app under test actually loaded.

Suggest asserting the negative over a window plus one positive check that the seeded state is live:

```swift
XCTAssertFalse(
    element("guided_first_session_hero_title").waitForExistence(timeout: 15),
    "Launch \(launch) must not admit migrated quiz state into the guided first session"
)
```

This matters more than usual because it's the regression proof the amended ONB-005 row in `REGRESSION_TESTING_PLAN.md` now points at, and because `AtlyUITests` never runs on PR checks — so nobody will catch a vacuous pass here from CI.

Commit c9fa0ad **addressed** this comment by replacing the synchronous `.exists` check with a 15-second negative wait and adding a positive assertion that the seeded unqualified-entry state is present. The fixture is also wired through the launch arguments and validated by helper tests.

Addressed in `c9fa0ad0b16aeae7de690ce13a062779e0c771fc`. The UI test now first waits for a test-only accessibility breadcrumb that is emitted only when the seeded migrated-state fixture resolves to `.fallback(.unqualifiedEntry)`, then waits the full 15-second hero-resolution window and asserts that the Hero never appears. This proves both fixture application and non-admission. Fresh exact-head native revalidation is queued; I am leaving the thread open until that proof returns.

Current-head proof has returned green for `c9fa0ad0b16aeae7de690ce13a062779e0c771fc`. `testEstablishedUserWithMigratedQuizStateNeverReentersGuidedFirstSession` passed **twice**; each invocation performed two internal launches, proved the positive unqualified-entry breadcrumb on every launch, and held the full 15-second Hero nonexistence window on every launch. The companion long-quiz/paywall/guided-search journey also passed twice. Durable native receipt SHA-256: `2b6f745d78e8c35f1d3fc5ef38b2b54c228ad55da613ca6aba65f364fba7856d`. Resolving this addressed thread.

### Unscoped marker admits wrong account `resolveHero` gates server-assigned guided first sessions on `personalizationService.hasQualifyingGuidedFirstSessionEntry()`, but that marker lives in `CodableStorage` on `UserDefaults.standard`, so it can survive logout/account switching and let account B qualify off account A’s stale `longQuizState` — should we clear the AtlyPlus keys in the logout/erase path? Want Baz to fix this for you? [Activate Fixer](https://baz.co/agents/baz)
Other fix methods
Prompt for AI Agents ```text Before applying, verify this suggestion against the current code. In Steps/Services/GuidedFirstSessionService.swift around lines 295-300 inside `resolveHero`, the new admission gate `isExplicitTestAssignment || personalizationService.hasQualifyingGuidedFirstSessionEntry()` can incorrectly pass after an account switch because the qualifying marker/`longQuizState` is persisted in UserDefaults (device-global) and may not be cleared on logout. Refactor so the persisted AtlyPlus personalization state is scoped to the active user/account (e.g., namespace the UserDefaults keys by account/user id) and/or store the account identifier alongside the marker and invalidate it in `hasQualifyingGuidedFirstSessionEntry()` when it doesn’t match the current account. Additionally, ensure the logout/account-switch path reliably clears the AtlyPlus personalization keys (or update `UserRepository.eraseCachedData()`/`AtlyPlusPersonalizationService.eraseCachedData()` to clear them) so stale data can’t satisfy this guard for the wrong account. ```

Commit 22f9c63 **addressed** this comment by wiring `AtlyPlusPersonalizationService` into the live logout cache-dependency list, ensuring its persisted quiz/admission state is erased during logout and cannot carry over to another account.

Addressed at exact PR head `22f9c636f1cd6d83217b933857d8d4877ea11729`. The existing `AtlyPlusPersonalizationService.eraseCachedData()` already clears `longQuizState`, the qualifying-entry marker, consumption, and retry state. This descendant now injects that service into `LogoutServiceKey.liveValue` and includes it in `LogoutServiceImpl` cache dependencies, so the logout cleanup loop actually invokes the erasure before another account can inherit those device-global values. Existing focused tests pin the service-level erase behavior; strict-descendant native revalidation remains required and pending.

### UI test burns 15s on negative `XCTAssertFalse(element("guided_first_session_hero_title").waitForExistence(timeout: 15), ...)` always burns the full 15s once the breadcrumb has appeared, and in the seeded `.fallback(.unqualifiedEntry)` path that hero is deterministically absent, so should we switch this to `waitForNonExistence(timeout: 1-2)` or a direct `XCTAssertFalse(element(...).exists)`? Want Baz to fix this for you? [Activate Fixer](https://baz.co/agents/baz) You can also update your AI coding guidelines based on this comment by `apply pr to [branch name]`
Other fix methods
Prompt for AI Agents ```text Before applying, verify this suggestion against the current code. In AtlyUITests/Flows/AtlyPlusOnboardingChromeTests.swift around lines 53-56, inside the established-user regression test where you assert the hero title is absent, you currently use XCTAssertFalse(element("guided_first_session_hero_title").waitForExistence(timeout: 15), ...). Refactor this to avoid waiting the full 15s for a negative condition: after the breadcrumb waitForExistence has already succeeded, either assert non-existence directly (e.g., element(...).exists is false) or use element(...).waitForNonExistence(timeout: 1–2). Keep the assertion message but make the timeout small/deterministic so the test doesn’t burn 15 seconds every launch. ```

### Warm-start leaks Atly Plus state The warm-start auto-login path in `RootViewModel` calls `dependencies.authRepository.logout()` directly instead of `LogoutService.logout()`, so `AtlyPlusPersonalizationService.eraseCachedData()` never runs and the previous account’s persisted Atly Plus state can carry into the new login — should we route that path through `LogoutService`? In Steps/AppServices/AppServices.swift around lines 150-152 within `LogoutServiceKey.liveValue`/`LogoutServiceImpl` cacheDependencies, you added `@Dependency(\.atlyPlusPersonalizationService)` but the warm-start auto-login path in `RootViewModel` still calls `dependencies.authRepository.logout()` directly and bypasses `LogoutService.logout()`. Refactor the warm-start logic so that any required pre-login logout (token-based authorization reset) goes through `LogoutService.logout()` (or a single shared logout coordinator) to ensure `AtlyPlusPersonalizationService.eraseCachedData()` always runs before routing to onboarding. Update the relevant `RootViewModel` code to remove the direct `authRepository.logout()` call (or have it delegate to `LogoutService`) and ensure the new-account context can’t inherit cached Atly Plus values. ```

Commit a02c678 **addressed** this comment by routing warm-start token login through `dependencies.logoutService.logout()` instead of directly calling `authRepository.logout()`, ensuring account-scoped cached state is erased.

The warm-start auto-login/account switching path in `RootViewModel` calls `dependencies.authRepository.logout()` directly, bypassing `dependencies.logoutService.logout()`, so `AtlyPlusPersonalizationService.eraseCachedData()` never runs and `hasQualifyingGuidedFirstSessionEntry` stays `true` — letting `GuidedFirstSessionService.resolveHero` re-enable guided-first-session eligibility from the previous account. However, `RootViewModel`'s warm-start auto-login/account-switching path bypasses `dependencies.logoutService.logout()` and calls `await dependencies.authRepository.logout()` directly, which only clears auth tokens and leaves `hasQualifyingGuidedFirstSessionEntry` unchanged, potentially leaking the prior account's personalization state into the next onboarding.
